messages:
Meera: Quick heads-up — Sales flagged a competitor feature: deterministic / "predictable responses" tier that customers are explicitly asking for. We need to decide if we build a parity tier or push a different differentiator.

Meera: Proposal: add a 'response-quality tiers' opt-in: parity-deterministic, standard (current), adaptive (ML-driven). Start with an MVP deterministic mode that pins sampling seeds, tight temperature control, and reduced non-deterministic postprocessing.

Jordan: +1 from AE side. A few enterprise pilots asked for EXACT reproducibility across requests for auditability. They want an SLA: same prompt => same answer 99.9% of the time.

Tess: From Solutions eng: customers will want both deterministic outputs and explanation of changes over model updates. That means we need model-version pinning + rollout audits.

Alex: Engineering concerns: deterministic mode implies we need to control RNG, cache behavior, and avoid server-side dedupers that introduce nondeterminism. Also for some models quantization + kernel scheduling can actually change float rounding and break determinism.

Sam: ML notes: true bit-exact determinism across hardware/quantization is hard. But we can provide deterministic-from-seed within a runtime variant: same model build, same env, same seed => reproducible. We should call it "reproducible tier" not absolute deterministic.

Meera: Agree on naming. For launch MVP we scope to: 1) hosted API only, 2) opt-in per-tenant flag, 3) pinned model version, 4) fixed RNG seed + temperature clamp, 5) rollout guardrails and eval set. Does that feel reasonable?

Alex: That scope is workable. Implementation notes: runtime flag to set RNG seed and disable "response smoothing" heuristics; ensure KV cache behavior is deterministic by ordering requests in the batch pipeline. Estimate 3 sprint work: runtime changes (2), eval harness + infra (1).

Sam: Evals: need a regression suite that compares outputs across builds. Example check: run 200 canonical prompts, compare token sequences. Fail if >0.1% token diffs. Also track semantic drift metrics.

Ruth: Launch criteria suggestion: (a) reproducibility pass on canonical eval (>= 99.9%), (b) performance impact <10% p50 latency, (c) cost uplift <20% for deterministic mode, (d) docs + sales enablement.

Jordan: Sales add-on: price this as a premium (auditability/compliance). Pilot with two existing enterprise pilots first.

Tess: One caveat — some customers want determinism but also higher creativity. We should allow per-route override for sampling params but warn that reproducibility guarantee then not supported.

Meera: Good call. I'll draft a short spec. Rough config example for API opt-in:
```json
{
  "response_tier": "reproducible",
  "seed": 42,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "model": "redwood-model-v3-2026",
  "pin_model_version": true
}
```

Alex: Nice. Implementation TODOs I see: runtime seed plumbing, deterministic batching order flag, quant/kernel checklist for supported model builds, and an eval CI job that runs nightly against pinned build.

Sam: We should also add a regression alert if semantic divergence > threshold after any model-rollout. That ties into Optimize quality monitoring.

Meera: Next steps: I'll put a short spec in the product repo and schedule a 30m sync with Eng + ML + Sales. Action items: Meera will draft spec (by Fri), Alex will surface engineering risks and estimate (by Mon), Sam will prepare eval plan and canonical prompt set (by Tue), Jordan will pick pilot customers.

deploy-bot: Reminder: please add the new spec doc to the product docs workspace for versioning.

Meera: Thanks all — we'll reconvene after initial estimates. :thumbsup:
